summary: In Greek mythology, Anaxibia (Ancient Greek Ἀναξιβία) is daughter of Bias and Iphianassa (niece of Melampus) and wife of Pelias at Iolcus. By him she bears Acastus and the daughters including Pisidice, Pelopia, Hippothoe, and Alcestis; some lists call her Alphesiboea or Phylomache instead.
etymology: Greek Ἀναξιβία; as Pelias' queen she is sometimes renamed Alphesiboea or Phylomache daughter of Amphion.

sections.heading: Wife of Pelias
paragraphs: Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 1.9.10) and Hyginus make Anaxibia daughter of Bias and wife of Pelias; their children include Acastus and Alcestis (later wife of Admetus), together with Pisidice, Pelopia, and Hippothoe. Theocritus and other strands preserve alternate queen-names for the same Iolcian marriage.
Through Acastus she stands behind the Peleus–Astydamia tragedy; through Alcestis she anchors the Pheraean house.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id anaxibia-pelias is Pelias' Biasid queen alone. Distinct from anaxibia-atreid (mother of Pylades), anaxibia-nestor, and the Danaid Anaxibia.
